{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=long-term+convergence+properties+of+path-dependent+preference+models+reinforcement+learning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1109/ictc66702.2025.11388608\", \"title\": [\"Reinforcement Learning-Based Correction of Indoor Path Loss Models for Wi-SUN Sub-GHz Communications\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/ictc66702.2025.11388608\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 10, 14]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7528788\", \"title\": [\"Solution Methods for Long-Term Debt Default Models: Convergence and Accuracy\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Long-term-debt default models are the workhorse of quantitative sovereign-debt research, yet the methods used to solve them have never been held to a common standard of accuracy. The difficulty is economic: the option to default makes the borrower&apos;s problem non-concave, and long maturities make the bond price a fixed point that feeds policy errors back into prices. We compare extreme-value taste shocks on a discrete menu with interpolated continuous-choice optimization in the Chatterjee and Eyigungor (2012) one-asset model and the Bianchi, Hatchondo and Martinez (2018) reserves model, both validated against the published replication outputs. First, smoothing the choice rule distorts primarily portfolio composition rather than leverage: reserves vary sharply with the taste-shock scale while mean debt barely moves—an error a one-asset model cannot exhibit. Second, convergence and accuracy are distinct. Borrower Euler residuals, lender pricing residuals, and a global menu-deviation audit reveal converged solutions that violate the model’s optimality conditions, a non-converged terminal iterate that matches converged candidates on the scored conditions, and matched moments—the literature’s usual check—that mask an order of magnitude in first-order accuracy. Third, taste shocks solve the portfolio model roughly three to four times faster than the continuous-choice reference at a small welfare cost, and a single post-solve re-optimization of the actions, repriced and re-evaluated, eliminates the measured welfare gap with the reference. An exact factorization of the pricing recursion contributes to the implementation’s speed.</jats:p>\",…

Abstract
Introduction
While AI-generated training recommendations may enhance the scientific rigor of competitive sports training, their use may also be associated with athletes’ autonomy in interpreting bodily states and making training decisions. Drawing on cognitive offloading theory, self-determination theory, and the appropriate reliance framework, this study examined a serial association model linking AI training recommendation dependence, body signal outsourcing tendency, reduced sense of self-regulation, training decision hesitation, and reduced training self-efficacy.
Methods
Cross-sectional questionnaire data were collected from 381 athletes. The hypothesized relationships were tested using structural equation modeling, bootstrap analyses of indirect associations, and multigroup analyses comparing athletes in physical-dominant and skill-dominant sports.

Computational Theories of Curiosity-Driven Learning
Pierre-Yves Oudeyer∗
Inria and Ensta ParisTech, France
Abstract
What are the functions of curiosity? What are the mechanisms of curiosity-driven learn-
ing? We approach these questions about the living using conc epts and tools from machine
learning and developmental robotics. We argue that curiosi ty-driven learning enables organ-
isms to make discoveries to solve complex problems with rare or deceptive rewards. By foster-
ing exploration and discovery of a diversity of behavioural skills, and ignoring these rewards,
curiosity can be efﬁcient to bootstrap learning when there i s no information, or deceptive in-
formation, about local improvement towards these problems . We also explain the key role
of curiosity for efﬁcient learning of world models. We revie w both normative and heuristic
computational frameworks used to understand the mechanism s of curiosity in humans, con-
ceptualizing the child as a sense-making organism. These fr ameworks enable us to discuss
the bi-directional causal links between curiosity and lear ning, and to provide new hypotheses
about the fundamental role of curiosity in self-organizing developmental structures through
curriculum learning. We present various developmental rob otics experiments that study these
mechanisms in action, both supporting these hypotheses to u nderstand better curiosity in hu-
mans and opening new research avenues in machine learning and artiﬁcial intelligence. Finally,
we discuss challenges for the design of experimental paradi gms for studying curiosity in psy-
chology and cognitive neuroscience.
Keywords: Curiosity, intrinsic motivation, world models, rewards, free-energy principle,
learning progress hypothesis, lifelong learning, predict ions, machine learning, AI, develop-
mental robotics, development, curriculum learning, self- organization.
